C218747: This section describes the investigational and noninvestigational trial interventions, including the rationale for dose selection, administration procedures, and concomitant therapy restrictions.
C218751: Exoticillin 500mg film-coated tablets. Nonproprietary name: exoticillin. Pharmaceutical dose form: film-coated tablet. Dosage strength: 500mg.
C218752: The dose of 500mg twice daily was selected based on Phase II data demonstrating optimal efficacy with an acceptable safety profile at this dose level.
C218753: Exoticillin 500mg tablets will be administered orally twice daily with or without food for the duration of the treatment period.
C218754: Dose reductions to 250mg twice daily are permitted for participants experiencing Grade 2 or higher adverse events attributable to the investigational product.
C218755: In the event of overdose, symptomatic and supportive treatment should be provided. There is no specific antidote for exoticillin.
C176274: Investigational product will be supplied as blister packs by the sponsor. No preparation is required at site.
C115525: Investigational product must be stored at room temperature (15-25°C), protected from light and moisture.
C176267: Site staff must maintain accurate records of all investigational product received, dispensed, and returned or destroyed.
C218756: Participants will be assigned to treatment using an Interactive Web Response System (IWRS).
C25196: Randomisation will be performed centrally using a 1:1 ratio via the IWRS. Randomisation will be stratified by disease severity and geographic region.
C189349: This is a double-blind trial. The investigational product and placebo are identical in appearance. The IWRS will maintain the blind.
C218757: Emergency unblinding may be performed by the investigator in the event of a medical emergency. The sponsor must be notified within 24 hours.
C218758: Adherence will be assessed by tablet count at each visit. Participants with less than 80% adherence will be counselled by site staff.
C218759: No noninvestigational trial interventions are planned for this trial.
C222329: Background therapy consists of standard-of-care treatment administered to all participants throughout the trial in addition to the investigational product.
C222330: Rescue therapy with short-acting bronchodilators is permitted for participants experiencing acute symptom exacerbation. Use of rescue therapy will be recorded in the eCRF.
C218761: No other noninvestigational trial interventions are planned. Any additional medications required for participant safety will be recorded as concomitant medications.
C53630: Concomitant medications taken within 30 days prior to screening and during the trial must be recorded in the electronic case report form.
C218762: The following medications are prohibited during the trial: strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, strong CYP3A4 inducers, and other investigational products.
C218763: All other concomitant medications are permitted provided they are stable for at least 30 days prior to randomisation.
